action: General advice: Expedia customers should be cautious with emails or texts about bookings or refunds, use a unique password with two-step login, and watch for an official Expedia statement.
date_note: Security Affairs, dated 14 November, is the earliest page read; no page gives the day of the claim itself.
exec: A very large but unverified data theft claim against a major travel platform, said to involve a third-party provider.
plain: A criminal group claims to have stolen nearly one billion Expedia traveller records. Expedia says attackers got in through an outside data provider but could not confirm the group's claims.

evidence.quote: Expedia investigates cyberattack after hackers claim theft of nearly 1 billion customer records

summary: A Russian extortion group calling itself n0n claims, per Security Affairs, to have stolen nearly one billion Expedia traveler records. Expedia told Skift attackers breached its systems through a third-party data platform provider, and told The Seattle Times the hackers' claims are unverified and it could not confirm their accuracy; its investigation continues. A law firm is weighing a possible class action, The Seattle Times reported.
title: Extortion group claims theft of nearly one billion Expedia traveler records

validation.note: Attacker claim reported by Security Affairs, Valley News Live and MyNorthwest; Expedia's statements (to Skift and The Seattle Times, as relayed) confirm a third-party provider compromise but not n0n's figures.

review.note: stronger than source: 'Russian-speaking' not on any page (now Russian per Security Affairs); claim vs Expedia-confirmed path attributed to Skift/Seattle Times; date_note, published day
